title: Newton's Laws of Motion and Friction
subject: physics

nodes.label: Newton's Laws of Motion and Friction
nodes.group: Newton's Laws of Motion and Friction
nodes.note: The three laws of motion, pseudo forces, constraint mechanics, and friction. JEE tests FBD isolation, elevator apparent weight, Atwood machines, and two-block friction thresholds.

nodes.label: Newton's Three Laws
nodes.note: The foundational laws of dynamics: inertia, force-momentum relation, and action-reaction.

nodes.label: First Law: Inertia
nodes.note: A body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force: $$\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = 0 \iff \vec{a} = 0$$. This defines inertial reference frames.

nodes.label: Second Law: F = ma
nodes.note: The net force equals the rate of change of momentum: $$\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}$$. For constant mass, $$\vec{F}_{\text{net}} = m\vec{a}$$.

nodes.label: Impulse-Momentum Theorem
nodes.note: The impulse of a force equals the change in momentum: $$\vec{J} = \int_{t_i}^{t_f} \vec{F}\,dt = \Delta\vec{p} = \vec{p}_f - \vec{p}_i$$. The area under an $$F$$-$$t$$ curve gives impulse.

nodes.label: Third Law: Action-Reaction
nodes.note: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction: $$\vec{F}_{AB} = -\vec{F}_{BA}$$. The pair acts on two different bodies simultaneously and can never cancel.

nodes.label: Action-Reaction Properties
nodes.note: Action and reaction act on distinct bodies, are simultaneous, share the same physical nature, and are collinear. They never act on the same body and never cancel each other.

nodes.label: Pseudo Force
nodes.note: In a non-inertial frame accelerating at $$\vec{a}_0$$, a fictitious force $$\vec{F}_{\text{pseudo}} = -m\vec{a}_0$$ must be introduced. It has no reaction partner and acts through the center of mass.

nodes.label: Apparent Weight in Elevator
nodes.note: In an elevator accelerating upward at $$a$$: $$N = m(g+a)$$. Accelerating downward: $$N = m(g-a)$$. In free fall: $$N = 0$$ (weightlessness).

nodes.label: Free Fall Weightlessness
nodes.note: When the elevator cable snaps ($$a = g$$ downward), the normal reaction vanishes: $$N = m(g-g) = 0$$. The passenger experiences apparent weightlessness.

nodes.label: Inertial Reference Frames
nodes.note: An inertial frame is one in which Newton's first law holds: an unforced particle maintains constant velocity. The ground frame is approximately inertial for JEE problems.

nodes.label: Constraints and Pulley Systems
nodes.note: String constraints, wedge contacts, Atwood machines, and spring dynamics with the sudden cut principle.

nodes.label: String Constraints
nodes.note: For an ideal massless inextensible string, the virtual work shortcut gives $$\sum \vec{T}_i \cdot \vec{a}_i = 0$$. This relates the accelerations of connected masses.

nodes.label: Movable Pulley
nodes.note: For a movable pulley with acceleration $$a_p$$ and connected masses with accelerations $$a_1$$ and $$a_2$$: $$a_p = \frac{a_1 + a_2}{2}$$.

nodes.label: Ideal String Assumptions
nodes.note: An ideal string is massless and inextensible. It cannot store energy, so the net work done by internal tension forces on the system is zero: $$\sum W_T = 0$$.

nodes.label: Wedge Contact Constraint
nodes.note: Two rigid bodies in contact cannot penetrate each other. The acceleration components perpendicular to the contact surface must match: $$a_{1,\perp} = a_{2,\perp}$$.

nodes.label: Atwood Machine
nodes.note: Two masses $$m_1 > m_2$$ connected by a light string over a frictionless pulley. The common acceleration is $$a = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$$ and tension is $$T = \frac{2m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$$.

nodes.label: Clamp Thrust
nodes.note: The thrust on the supporting pulley clamp is $$F_{\text{clamp}} = 2T = \frac{4m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$$. This is strictly less than the total weight $$(m_1 + m_2)g$$.

nodes.label: Spring Dynamics
nodes.note: Hooke's law gives the restoring force $$\vec{F}_s = -k\vec{x}$$. The product $$k \cdot L$$ is constant for a given spring, so cutting changes stiffness.

nodes.label: Sudden Cut Principle
nodes.note: When a string is cut, tension drops instantaneously: $$T(0^+) = 0$$. A spring force cannot change instantaneously: $$F_s(0^+) = F_s(0^-)$$.

nodes.label: Series and Parallel Springs
nodes.note: Series: $$\frac{1}{k_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{1}{k_1} + \frac{1}{k_2}$$. Parallel: $$k_{\text{eq}} = k_1 + k_2$$.

nodes.label: Virtual Work Method
nodes.note: Since ideal strings cannot store energy, the net work done by internal tensions is zero: $$\sum \vec{T}_i \cdot \vec{v}_i = 0$$. This gives constraint relations between accelerations.

nodes.label: Friction Mechanics
nodes.note: Static and kinetic friction laws, angle of friction, angle of repose, and optimal pulling force.

nodes.label: Static Friction
nodes.note: Static friction is self-adjusting: $$0 \le f_s \le f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N$$. It matches the applied tangential force up to the limiting value.

nodes.label: Kinetic Friction
nodes.note: Once sliding begins, $$f_k = \mu_k N$$ where $$\mu_k \le \mu_s$$. Kinetic friction is nearly independent of sliding speed and contact area.

nodes.label: Direction of Kinetic Friction
nodes.note: Kinetic friction opposes the relative motion between the two contacted surfaces, not the absolute motion. On a two-block system, friction on the top block can act forward.

nodes.label: Angle of Friction
nodes.note: The angle of friction is $$\lambda = \tan^{-1}\mu_s$$. The total contact force is $$R = \sqrt{N^2 + f^2}$$ and ranges from $$N$$ to $$N\sqrt{1 + \mu_s^2}$$.

nodes.label: Total Contact Force
nodes.note: The resultant contact force $$\vec{R} = \vec{N} + \vec{f}$$ makes angle $$\lambda$$ with the normal when friction is at its limiting value: $$\tan\lambda = \frac{f_{s,\max}}{N} = \mu_s$$.

nodes.label: Angle of Repose
nodes.note: The maximum incline angle for static equilibrium is $$\theta_r = \tan^{-1}\mu_s = \lambda$$. At this angle, $$mg\sin\theta_r = \mu_s mg\cos\theta_r$$.

nodes.label: Acceleration Down Incline
nodes.note: For $$\theta > \theta_r$$, the body accelerates down: $$a = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta)$$. For $$\theta < \theta_r$$, static friction holds it at rest.

nodes.label: Minimum Pulling Force
nodes.note: To pull a block on a rough horizontal surface with force $$F$$ at angle $$\theta$$: $$F = \frac{\mu mg}{\cos\theta + \mu\sin\theta}$$. The minimum occurs at $$\theta = \lambda$$.

nodes.label: Minimum Pull Value
nodes.note: The minimum pulling force is $$F_{\min} = \frac{\mu mg}{\sqrt{1 + \mu^2}} = mg\sin\lambda$$, achieved when the pull angle equals the angle of friction.

nodes.label: Nature of Friction
nodes.note: Friction is an electromagnetic contact force that opposes relative sliding or the tendency of relative sliding. It is independent of apparent contact area.

nodes.label: Two-Block Friction Systems
nodes.note: Friction between two blocks with external force applied to either the top or bottom block. The slipping threshold depends on which block is pulled.

nodes.label: Force on Top Block
nodes.note: When force $$F$$ is applied to the top block $$m_1$$ on bottom block $$m_2$$ (smooth floor), the maximum acceleration of $$m_2$$ without slipping is $$a_{B,\max} = \frac{\mu m_1 g}{m_2}$$.

nodes.label: Top Pull Threshold
nodes.note: The threshold force for slipping is $$F_{\text{th}} = \mu m_1 g\left(1 + \frac{m_1}{m_2}\right)$$. Below this, both blocks move together at $$a = \frac{F}{m_1 + m_2}$$.

nodes.label: Force on Bottom Block
nodes.note: When force $$F$$ is applied to the bottom block $$m_2$$, the top block $$m_1$$ is accelerated only by friction. The maximum acceleration of $$m_1$$ without slipping is $$a_{A,\max} = \mu g$$.

nodes.label: Bottom Pull Threshold
nodes.note: The threshold force for slipping is $$F_{\text{th}} = \mu(m_1 + m_2)g$$. Below this, both blocks move together; above this, $$m_1$$ slides at constant $$a = \mu g$$.

nodes.label: Slipping Regimes
nodes.note: Below threshold, both blocks move with common acceleration. Above threshold, the pulled block accelerates independently while the other moves at constant friction-limited acceleration.

nodes.label: Friction as Accelerator
nodes.note: In the bottom-pull case, friction on the top block acts forward, accelerating it in the direction of motion. Friction is not always a retarding force.

nodes.label: Maximum Friction Force
nodes.note: The maximum friction force available between two blocks is $$f_{\max} = \mu m_1 g$$ where $$m_1$$ is the top block. This limits the acceleration that friction can transmit.
